clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms at the close of Saturday, December 30, 1933, the second of the two closing days. The dossier holds no own-terms record for this order, so the end cites the order's complete registered text, which contains the stated period.

research_rationale:
EO 6516 (December 20, 1933, Franklin D. Roosevelt). Text and identity: read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-28: the APP page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/(MIRROR_)DOCUMENTS.jsonl has a heading naming this order number, a date and subject agreeing with the held text, and a text_sha256 equal to the held file's. Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. It closes the executive departments and independent establishments in the District of Columbia, including the Government Printing Office and the Navy Yard and stations, on Saturday, December 23, 1933 and Saturday, December 30, 1933, and excuses federal employees there from duty on those days, except those excepted for special public reasons or whose absence would conflict with existing law. The recital of appreciation for the employees' service is not a command. First end: by its own terms at the close of 1933-12-30, the second and last day it governs (the December 23 part was spent at the close of that day). Searches: census titles and type rows, the WPA 1944 list (1933 closings) and a full-text citation search found no later order naming EO 6516; the census hit EO 6559 (1934) concerns banks and a different proclamation of December 30, 1933.
